title: Formulary Assignment Status from Enrollment to Termination
content:
Under the Formulary Benefit, the formulary assignment follows the member's plan enrollment. It opens with the enrollment, takes effect on the enrollment's effective date, ends on its coverage end date, and is restored by a COBRA reinstatement.

## Statuses

| Status | Meaning | Moves to |
|---|---|---|
| pending effective | the assignment is open, and the coverage effective date has not been reached | active, when the effective date is reached; terminated, when the future-dated enrollment is cancelled before it takes effect |
| active | the formulary governs the member's claims | terminated, when plan coverage ends |
| terminated | plan coverage has ended or was cancelled | active, on a COBRA reinstatement of the plan enrollment |

All of these moves are made by the system from the plan enrollment. When an assignment is opened, its effective date and its transition start date are both the plan coverage effective date. On termination the last day of coverage is recorded as the end date. On reinstatement the end date is cleared, because coverage continues.

## Rules tied to status

- No exception is decided, and no transition fill is allowed, for a date of service on which the assignment is not active.
- Exception approvals already in force when coverage ends lapse with the coverage. On a COBRA reinstatement they resume through their original expiration date.

*Hypothetical.* A member's coverage ends on 31 May while an approval runs to 30 September, and a COBRA reinstatement restores the enrollment on 20 June. From 1 June the approval has lapsed. Once the member is reinstated it resumes, and it still expires on 30 September.
